title: VPC connection risk thermometer + mitigation playbook (Console)
creator: Sofia Garcia
description:
Problem: Operators managing Private/VPC clusters need a quick, action-oriented surface in the Console that communicates the current risk level of cluster-to-cluster and tenant egress connectivity, explains probable causes, and shows recommended mitigations (both automated and operator-driven). Current status pages and network views are too forensic — they require reading logs or drilling into topology maps to understand impact and next steps.

Goal: Design a compact, persistent "connection risk" card (thermometer-style) at the cluster and tenant level that summarizes risk with graded states (green/ok, amber/degraded, red/critical), shows contributing signals (latency spikes, packet loss, route flaps, peering errors), and surfaces prescriptive playbook steps with one-click actions (run traceroute, toggle rollback, open support ticket). The UI must scale between single-cluster detail and multi-cluster ops views.

Scope: Console components (cluster overview, tenant detail, Ops command center). Deliverables: wireframes for card + hover expansion, high-fidelity components for cluster detail page, prototype with live data toggles for usability testing, accessibility checklist, handoff-ready specs for Eng (variant states, animation timings, data contract).

Out-of-scope: Full topology visualizer (separate epic), backend signal aggregation implementation (ENG work), incident timeline replay (existing feature).

Design principles: "Action-first" (show next step), "Confidence with context" (small set of signals with confidence score), "Progressive disclosure" (compact summary with expandable playbook). Prioritize clarity under stressful incident conditions: no ambiguous colors, non-blocking CTAs, keyboard-first interactions.
acceptance_criteria: Connection risk card appears on Cluster Overview and Tenant Detail pages with correct state mapping (green/amber/red) based on sample signal inputs.
Hover/expand shows top 3 contributing signals with timestamps and a confidence score for each.
Playbook lists ≥3 recommended mitigations for amber and ≥5 for red, with at least one automated quick-action where backend stub exists.
Usability test (n=6 ops engineers) median task completion time for identifying mitigation < 90s.
All UI elements meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast; keyboard navigation and screen reader labels documented.
Handoff spec includes component tokens, states, micro-interaction notes, and API field contract (list of signals with severity/confidence/date).
review_notes: 2026-02-25 - PM review (Liam Patel): +1 on action-first. Asked to include cost-estimate badge when recommended mitigation involves cross-region failover.
2026-03-02 - Eng design review (Priya Rao): Recommend reducing animation complexity for 200ms mobile and embeddable console builds; flagged need for an API field 'signal_confidence' (float 0..1).
2026-03-05 - Security (Alex Novak): Requested formal review if quick-action includes 'open-support-ticket' autofill with tenant data (privacy requirement).
2026-03-09 - Usability lab (3 ops, 3 SREs): participants preferred thermometer + numeric score over only color band. Adjusted to show both color + percentage confidence.

Decision 2026-03-10: Use compact thermometer with numeric confidence, include optional cost badge, and ship quick-action stubs behind feature flag 'net-quick-actions'. Security review required before enabling autofill in customer-facing tickets.
